title: China Removes General Who Commanded Forces at Doklam and Galwan
excerpt: General Zhao Zongqi, who reportedly authorized the 2020 Galwan operation to 'teach India a lesson,' has been expelled from China's top political advisory body as Xi Jinping's military purge widens.
body:
• General Zhao Zongqi, former commander of the PLA's Western Theatre Command during the 2017 Doklam standoff and the 2020 Galwan Valley clash, has been removed from China's top political advisory body.
  • Zhao reportedly authorized the Galwan operation to "teach India a lesson," according to a 2020 report citing US intelligence sources.
  • His removal is part of Xi Jinping's sweeping military purge that has sidelined over 100 senior officers since 2022, leaving only two active members on the seven-seat Central Military Commission.
  • The purge of the Western Theatre Command's former leadership raises questions about command stability along India's border with China.

Chinese General Zhao Zongqi, who commanded the People's Liberation Army forces during two of the most dangerous India-China border confrontations in decades, has been expelled from China's top political advisory body. State-run Xinhua news agency reported that Zhao was stripped of his membership in the Chinese People's Political Consultative Conference (CPPCC) and removed from two other positions.

Beijing did not provide a reason for the removal or announce any formal investigation against Zhao. The move comes as President Xi Jinping's years-long purge of the PLA reaches deep into the military's senior ranks, sweeping aside commanders, procurement officials, and defense industry executives.

The General Behind Doklam and Galwan

Zhao served as the first commander of the PLA's Western Theatre Command after Xi Jinping personally handed him the military flag in 2016. The command oversees Chinese military operations across Tibet and Xinjiang and along the country's extensive border with India.

Both the 73-day Doklam standoff in 2017 — a tense trilateral confrontation between India, China, and Bhutan at a strategically sensitive tri-junction — and the deadly Galwan Valley clash in June 2020 occurred under Zhao's command. The Galwan confrontation on June 15, 2020, resulted in the deaths of 20 Indian soldiers in hand-to-hand combat along the Line of Actual Control in eastern Ladakh.

"Zhao authorised the Galwan operation to 'teach India a lesson.'"

— 2020 ANI report, citing US intelligence sources

According to that report, Zhao had overseen previous standoffs with India and was concerned that China should not appear weak before the United States and its allies, including India. He was replaced as Western Theatre commander in December 2020 after reaching retirement age. Born in 1955 in Heilongjiang Province, Zhao had combat experience dating back to the Sino-Vietnamese War and was once the youngest commander among the PLA's seven military regions.

Xi's Unprecedented Military Purge

Zhao's removal is the latest in a campaign that analysts have called the most significant military purge since the death of Mao Zedong in 1976. Since 2022, over 100 senior PLA officers have been swept aside or gone missing.

The most dramatic actions came in January 2026, when General Zhang Youxia — the PLA's most senior uniformed officer and CMC vice chairman — and General Liu Zhenli, chief of the Joint Staff Department, were placed under investigation for "suspected serious violations of discipline and law." Their removal from the Central Military Commission left only two active members on the previously seven-member body: Xi himself and General Zhang Shengmin, the commission's disciplinary chief.

The purge has also extended into China's defense industry. Former defense industry regulator Zhang Jianhua was sentenced to 10 years in prison for bribery earlier this month, while Ma Xingrui, former chief of Xinjiang province, was expelled from the Communist Party in July.

What It Means for India's Border Security

For India and the Indian diaspora — which followed the Doklam and Galwan crises closely — the purge of commanders associated with the Western Theatre Command carries strategic significance. The systematic removal of senior military leaders raises questions about PLA command continuity along one of the world's most contested borders.

The instability at the top of China's military hierarchy could cut both ways: it may distract Beijing from border provocations, but it could also leave decision-making in the hands of less experienced officers eager to prove loyalty to Xi. India's defense establishment will be watching closely to see whether the turmoil affects PLA deployments and posture along the Line of Actual Control.
